title: Review afterglow notes — async flow & small refactors
content:
Context:
- Quick capture after reviewing PR #4217 (async batching + small API change). Author: Marco. Size: medium (14 files). Goal: reduce tail latency for concurrent short requests and remove a legacy feature-flag path.

High-level impressions:
- Nice: clear tests for batching behavior, CI includes perf job. Good commit messages for the core algorithm change.
- Concern: a few noisy TODO stubs left in production code (not gated) and one POSSIBLE race in the cache invalidation path.
- Risk: change touches hot path (request-handler -> batcher -> kernel-selector). Wrong rollback would impact p95.

Immediate actions (short checklist, for merge readiness):
- [ ] Get a second +1 from SRE (concurrency/race check). Suggested reviewer: Tanya.
- [ ] Replace inline TODOs with explicit // FIXME + issue link or remove before merge.
- [ ] Add assertion in batcher that sequence_id never decreases (quick defensive test).
- [ ] Add a stress test in perf harness (5k short requests/sec, 1–2 tokens) — capture p50/p95/p99.
- [ ] Confirm metrics emitted for fallback path (metric name: runtime.batcher.fallback_count).
- [ ] Add a rollback plan in PR description (which commit to revert + smoke test).

Observations & micro TODOs (notes to self):
- Line in batcher (batch_manager.py:216) uses list.pop(0) — O(n) for big contiguous ops. Consider deque.
- The gating of legacy feature_flag_experiment looks like it can be removed early; but leave a flag in config for 2 weeks with telemetry to detect any user regressions. Add telemetry: gauge user-facing latency per model variant.
- kernel_selector changes: switched heuristics to prefer memory-compact kernels for short sequences. Need to ensure quantized kernels have same output shape. Add unit test to compare outputs (float v quantized) for small seed inputs.
- cache invalidation: potential race when two threads call invalidate(prefix) concurrently. Hypothesis: missing lock in kv_cache.py -> invalidate(). Add an integration test that runs parallel invalidations.

Refactor sketch (low-effort, medium-impact):
- Problem: request_handler contains both orchestration and sanity-check logic. Hard to test.
- Proposal: extract small facade `RequestSanitizer` that runs validations (seq length, token budget, policy checks) before handing off to BatchManager. Keep it internal (no public API change). Benefits: easier unit-testing, reduces cognitive load in handler.
- Implementation plan (estimate 1.5d):
  - Create RequestSanitizer class + tests (0.5d)
  - Wire into handler with feature flag off by default (0.25d)
  - Flip flag after green perf and integration tests + monitor (0.75d)

Refactor sketch (bigger idea, backlog):
- Split batch_manager responsibilities into: BatchCoordinator (scheduling/combining) and BatchLifecycle (eviction, TTL, metrics). This will help for Dedicated workloads where lifecycle needs tenant isolation. Estimate: 3–5d.

Rollback & rollout plan (required):
- Canary rollout: 5% of traffic for 24h, capture p95, error-rate, fallback_count. If p95 regresses >10% or error-rate >0.2% -> revert.
- Backout commit: add explicit revert commit in PR notes (commit sha). Also ensure monitoring playbook has runbook links.

Questions for the author (to add as PR comments):
1) Why was list.pop(0) used — perf vs earlier semantics?
2) Can we add a simple docstring for kernel selector heuristics (mapping to HW)?
3) Is there a reason the cache.invalidate API is public to callers outside kv layer?

Follow-ups (owners & deadlines):
- Marco: add stress perf test and update PR (due 2025-02-06).
- Marco + Tanya: pair on concurrency test for cache invalidate (due 2025-02-07).
- Odette: land small RequestSanitizer refactor in a follow-up PR once this one is stable (TBD after canary).
- Eng-SRE: prepare dashboard for batcher.fallback_count and kernel_selector decisions (owner: SRE oncall rotation).

Notes on testing strategy (practical):
- Unit: sanity checks for all new branches in kernel selector, kv_cache lock test.
- Integration: run full regression — endpoints smoke, then run short-sequence stress harness.
- Perf: use existing perf pipeline with short/short+long mixed to capture whether batching harms long requests.

Random ideas/brain dump (might be useful later):
- Introduce a small sampling tracer that records per-request path through kernel_selector (tiny percent sample) — helps postmortems.
- Consider exposing a model/variant hint to clients so batching can be more effective (client opt-in). Privacy implications: low, but doc this.

Quick checklist before marking PR ready-for-merge: 
- [ ] SRE sign-off recorded in PR
- [ ] Stress perf numbers in PR comment (p50/p95/p99)
- [ ] All TODOs removed or converted to tracked issues
- [ ] Canary plan added to PR description
- [ ] Rollback commit noted

Last-minute thought: try to keep this change additive and small — any reordering of the kernel selection pipeline increases cognitive surface for oncall. If we need to revert quickly, prefer a toggled config instead of immediate behavior flip.

-- Odette (after reviewing PR #4217)
